your account's base URL, https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com, shown in the Infobip API Resource hub — it identifies the account, the key authenticates it

example_prompt: Fetch the latest SMS delivery reports from Infobip when a webhook isn't available, to confirm whether messages were delivered.

bulkId.description: The ID that uniquely identifies the request. Bulk ID will be received only when you send a message to more than one destination address. Passed as a query parameter.

messageId.description: The ID that uniquely identifies the message sent. Passed as a query parameter.

limit.description: Maximum number of delivery reports to be returned. If not set, the latest 50 records are returned. Maximum limit value is 1000 and you can only access reports for the last 48h. Passed as a query parameter.

entityId.description: Entity id used to send the message. For more details, see our [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management). Passed as a query parameter.

applicationId.description: Application id used to send the message. For more details, see our [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management). Passed as a query parameter.

campaignReferenceId.description: ID of a campaign that was sent in the message. Passed as a query parameter.

results.description: Collection of reports, one per every message.

items.description: Collection of reports, one per every message.

bulkId.description: Unique ID assigned to the request if messaging multiple recipients or sending multiple messages via a single API request.

currency.description: The currency in which the price is expressed.

status.description: Indicates the [status](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#api-status-codes) of the message and how to recover from an error should there be any.

groupName.description: Status group name that describes which category the status code belongs to, i.e., [PENDING](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#pending-general-status-codes), [UNDELIVERABLE](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#undeliverable-general-status-codes), [DELIVERED](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#delivered-general-status-codes), [EXPIRED](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#expired-general-status-codes), [REJECTED](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#rejected-general-status-codes).

action.description: Action to take to recover from the error.

error.description: Indicates whether an [error](https://www.infobip.com/docs/essentials/response-status-and-error-codes#error-codes) occurred during the query execution.

groupName.description: Error group name that describes which category the error code belongs to.

permanent.description: Indicates whether the error is recoverable or not.

sender.description: The sender ID which can be alphanumeric or numeric (e.g., `CompanyName`).

sentAt.description: Date and time when the message was sent. Has the following format: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ.

doneAt.description: Date and time when the Infobip services finished processing the message (i.e., delivered to the destination, network, etc.). Has the following format: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ.

callbackData.description: Callback data sent through ‛callbackData‛ field when sending message.

platform.description: Platform options. For more details, see [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

entityId.description: Used when specifying an entity in outbound send requests. It is also returned in notification events. For detailed usage, refer to the [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

applicationId.description: Used when specifying an application in outbound send requests. It is also returned in notification events. For detailed usage, refer to the [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

campaignReferenceId.description: ID of a campaign that was sent in the message.

gotchas: Send the API key as 'Authorization: App <API_KEY>' — the prefix App; Bearer is only for OAuth 2.0 access tokens. Infobip API keys have a predefined expiry date and can be revoked at any time; a missing or invalid credential answers 401.
The OpenAPI lists these API key scopes for this endpoint (x-scopes): message:send, sms:message:send, sms:manage. Give the key a matching scope when you create it.

Each Infobip account has its own base URL, xxxxx.api.infobip.com, shown once you log in to the Infobip API Resource hub. Set it in INFOBIP_BASE_URL (https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com in this spec is a placeholder). It identifies your account, the API key authenticates it.
Each report is returned only once: store it as soon as you fetch it. If the status changes again later, a new report for the new status comes in a later call.
Only the last 48 hours are available; limit defaults to 50 and caps at 1000 per call.
This endpoint is the fallback for when you can't receive reports on a webhook (webhooks.delivery.url in send_sms).

The OpenAPI documents no error body for this endpoint (401, 403, 500 have no schema): handle errors on the HTTP status. The 401 body shown on the authentication page is { requestError: { serviceException: { messageId, text } } }.
